title: Day cycle controller
brief: Time of day controller for the Kevnnard 3D room. Auto mode starts from the local PC time and advances one simulated minute per real second (60×, a full day in 24 minutes). Shows simulated time and PC time separately, Day/Sunset/Night presets, pause/resume, and a manual range; manual input pauses auto until resumed. Auto, manual and pause are proposed affordances.

artboards.title: Orbital clock
artboards.tradeoff: Large 24-hour dial makes day/night position instantly readable and drag feels physical; the side panel takes about 440px of width from the room, and fine minute control relies on the range below the dial.

artboards.title: Timeline dock
artboards.tradeoff: Full-width 24-hour strip shows phases, the simulated playhead and the PC-time marker side by side, plus a countdown to the next phase; the dock permanently claims the bottom band of the viewport and reads more like a media player than part of the room.

artboards.title: Compact console
artboards.tradeoff: Smallest footprint: a corner instrument that collapses to a one-line pill and leaves the room almost untouched, with offset and day progress for precise readers; the monospace density is less discoverable and less playful for first-time visitors.
